headline: 7 Bangladeshis killed in Kolkata hotel fire, leaseholder arrested
summary: Two more victims from Satkhira have been identified, bringing the total number of confirmed Bangladeshi deaths to seven in the devastating blaze.
details: A devastating fire at Hotel Shikha Inn in Kolkata, India, has claimed the lives of at least nine people, including seven confirmed Bangladeshi nationals.
The latest victims identified are Alimuzzaman Saju, 48, and Rebati Sarkar, 35, both residents of Kaliganj, Satkhira. Both had traveled to India for medical treatment.
Other victims include a family of four from Kushtia—Debashish Dutta, Afsana Sharmin, their three-year-old son Swarnashish, and Akram Ali—as well as Ahmed Babu from Savar, Dhaka.
Following the tragedy, the leaseholder of the hotel has been arrested, and two employees have been detained for questioning by Indian authorities.
The Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata has opened a helpline (91 8274821352) to assist families and provide information.
Local police in Satkhira are working to collect detailed information as families await the return of the bodies of their loved ones.
caption:
7 Bangladeshis confirmed dead after a devastating hotel fire in Kolkata. The leaseholder has been arrested.

A devastating fire at Hotel Shikha Inn in Kolkata, India, has claimed the lives of at least nine people, including seven confirmed Bangladeshi nationals.

The latest victims identified are Alimuzzaman Saju, 48, and Rebati Sarkar, 35, both residents of Kaliganj, Satkhira. Both had traveled to India for medical treatment.

Other victims include a family of four from Kushtia—Debashish Dutta, Afsana Sharmin, their three-year-old son Swarnashish, and Akram Ali—as well as Ahmed Babu from Savar, Dhaka.

Following the tragedy, the leaseholder of the hotel has been arrested, and two employees have been detained for questioning by Indian authorities.

The Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata has opened a helpline (91 8274821352) to assist families and provide information.

Local police in Satkhira are working to collect detailed information as families await the return of the bodies of their loved ones.

headline_marked: Trump vows [[tremendous economic costs]] for countries helping Iran
headline: Trump vows tremendous economic costs for countries helping Iran
summary: The US President has announced a 'crushing' economic operation to isolate the Islamic republic, threatening sanctions on any nation doing business with it.
details: US President Donald Trump announced a major new campaign to target Iran's economy, threatening 'tremendous' punishment on any country that provides a lifeline to the Islamic republic.
Trump described the move as the 'most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country,' calling it economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale.
The US Treasury's 'Operation Economic Fury' aims to cut off Iran's funding by targeting oil smuggling, cash transfers, exchange houses, and front companies.
This escalation comes as the conflict enters its sixth month, with the Strait of Hormuz remaining significantly choked-off and diplomatic off-ramps unseen.
The UAE has already suspended all economic dealings with Iran after being targeted by two ballistic missiles, signaling a shift in regional dynamics.
While Trump claimed US military efforts are facilitating the transit of ships through the Strait, reports suggest traffic is only at half of pre-war volumes.
Iran remains defiant, with some US media reports suggesting the conflict has severely drawn down US munition stockpiles, though the Pentagon has denied this.
caption:
Trump warns of 'tremendous economic consequences' for any nation doing business with Iran.

US President Donald Trump announced a major new campaign to target Iran's economy, threatening 'tremendous' punishment on any country that provides a lifeline to the Islamic republic.

Trump described the move as the 'most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country,' calling it economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale.

The US Treasury's 'Operation Economic Fury' aims to cut off Iran's funding by targeting oil smuggling, cash transfers, exchange houses, and front companies.

This escalation comes as the conflict enters its sixth month, with the Strait of Hormuz remaining significantly choked-off and diplomatic off-ramps unseen.

The UAE has already suspended all economic dealings with Iran after being targeted by two ballistic missiles, signaling a shift in regional dynamics.

While Trump claimed US military efforts are facilitating the transit of ships through the Strait, reports suggest traffic is only at half of pre-war volumes.

Iran remains defiant, with some US media reports suggesting the conflict has severely drawn down US munition stockpiles, though the Pentagon has denied this.
